newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures erode late, close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures erode late, close mostly lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures eroded again in late trading, with most units closing with small to moderate losses.
March Treasury bond futures dipped again on closing dealer sales and finished on the day's low after thin trading.
Some brokers tied the renewed slippage to somewhat softer results than expected for the two-year Treasury note auction, coupled with more signs of technical selling.
The two-year note fetched a high yield of 5.874 percent against some forecasts for 5.87 percent. The bid/cover ratio was 2.23, while non-competitive bids totaled $1.34 billion.
"It was a little disappointing, plus you're setting up for the five-year (note auction)," said one T-bond futures broker.
Treasury will sell $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Thursday, and one floor analyst reminded that the five-year maturity typically proves more difficult to place than the two-year note.
The final decline pushed March T-bonds to a close below the 112-08/32 level, although brokers debated the significance of that action given the thinness of the market.
"It's not a great close," said the broker. "Typically, we'd have to say the market's going to roll over (fall)."

"But given the thinness of the market...it's a question of whether you should sell weakness at the lower part of the range -- (or) should you be buying it down here?" he added. "You'd probably be a little safer buying it."
On Thursday, weekly jobless claims are seen rising to 331,000 from 317,000. The December Philadelphia Federal Reserve survey is expected at 7.4 versus 6.4.

At settlement, March T-bonds ended down 15/32 at 112-02/32, 10-year notes lost 9/32 to 108-31/32, muni-bonds dropped 6/32 to 114-30/32, T-bills eased two bps to 94.94, and March Eurodollars closed off one bp at 94.42. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
